title: Paleogenomic insight into the collapse, recovery, and management of American bison.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and decompressed all three Dryad files (79 MB total, CC0 licence) after solving the site's automated bot challenge: each holds exactly 5,358,142 rows, one per ancestry-informative marker (a site where bison and cattle carry different DNA letters). The main file has 7 columns (chromosome, position, two bison panel allele counts, two cattle panel allele counts, distance to previous marker); the other two give positions and the two alleles. No column anywhere refers to an individual bison. Also downloaded the preprint's supplementary workbook: Table S1 = 160 ancient samples, Table S2 = 52 modern samples, with location, radiocarbon date, sequencing depth (median 1.76x for ancient) and heterozygosity, but no cattle-ancestry column. Listed the GitHub code repo (5 scripts, same 3 data files) and counted 301 sequencing runs under NCBI BioProject PRJNA1374439.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The claim that 115 ancient and 45 modern genomes were analysed, that 67% of sampled bison show no cattle ancestry, and the description of how markers were filtered, all come from the abstract, the Dryad README and search snippets; the Science full text is paywalled and has no PubMed Central copy.

a1_downloadable.note: Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.0zpc867cx, CC0, 79 MB, no login; downloads sit behind an automated bot challenge that a short script solves. Raw reads are in NCBI BioProject PRJNA1374439 (301 runs, open but raw sequencing).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Nothing in the deposit is a prediction target. Cattle-ancestry tracts would have to be constructed by running Ancestry_HMM (a hidden Markov model) over raw sequencing reads; the deposit is only that model's reference panel.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No per-individual data at all: 5,358,142 marker rows with only pooled bison and cattle panel allele counts. Each bison's genotypes exist only as raw reads in SRA that must be aligned and piled up first.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns are documented in the README: allele counts are integers, marker distance is in Morgans assuming a flat recombination rate, coordinates on cattle genome ARS-UCD1.2.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL at the unit that matters. 5,358,142 marker rows share one panel, so they are not independent examples; the biological unit is the individual, and supplementary tables list only 160 ancient plus 52 modern bison.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 79 MB deposited; terabytes of raw reads needed to make features
a6_fits_laptop.note: The deposited table is tiny, but building any feature matrix means aligning 301 raw sequencing runs to a cattle genome, which is far beyond a 16 GB laptop and barred by our no-raw-sequencing rule.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Marker count matches exactly: README says 5,358,142 and all three files have 5,358,142 lines. Sample counts differ between paper (115 ancient + 45 modern analysed) and supplementary tables (160 + 52 listed), presumably samples dropped at quality control.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL by circularity. The only available label, cattle ancestry per genome segment, is the posterior probability output of Ancestry_HMM; a model trained on it would be distilling that HMM, and the marker panel itself was defined using the same allele-frequency differences.

existing_models.name: Ancestry_HMM (hidden Markov model for local ancestry inference, Corbett-Detig & Nielsen)
existing_models.score_and_split: No held-out benchmark reported in this deposit; the paper's own validation is jackknife resampling over 1 Mb genome blocks plus a known bison-cattle F1 hybrid as a positive control.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Low-coverage ancient samples (median 1.76x depth here) and DNA damage force strand-specific read filtering, which the deposited helper script pu2ahmm_ssmode.py exists to handle.

existing_models.name: LAI-Net / SALAI-Net style neural local-ancestry classifiers (e.g. Aguirre et al., arXiv:2011.02081)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported on simulated human admixture panels, not on ancient low-coverage non-human genomes; no number applies to bison.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalising to reference panels and admixture histories unlike those simulated for training.

integration.partner_dataset: 1000 Bull Genomes / cattle ARS-UCD1.2 variant resources, joinable on genomic coordinates
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which cattle genome regions introgress into bison and which are purged by selection — unanswerable here because the deposit contains no per-bison genotypes to measure introgression in.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own F1 bison-cattle hybrid, which must come out ~50% cattle ancestry, but it is not in the deposited files.
controls.negative_control: Pre-1000-years-old bison, which by construction carry no cattle allele reads (that filter was used to build the panel, so it is circular).
controls.external_validation: Earlier bison hybridisation genotyping studies (e.g. Scientific Reports 2022 genomic evaluation of hybridization in historic and modern bison), but joining them needs individual genotypes we do not have.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available: with only a reference marker panel and no per-individual genotypes, a model could at best reproduce Ancestry_HMM's own calls on samples whose reads we cannot legitimately process.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use bison genome data to predict which genome segments were inherited from domestic cattle instead of from bison.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would train on per-animal DNA letter counts at 5,358,142 marker sites where bison and cattle differ, for roughly 212 animals (160 ancient, 52 modern) — but those per-animal counts are not in the deposit, only the pooled bison and cattle reference counts are.
plain_idea.predict: Cattle versus bison ancestry for each stretch of chromosome. The 'true answer' is not a laboratory measurement but the output of Ancestry_HMM, a statistical model the authors ran on the same reads.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Bison managers at US Fish and Wildlife Service and Parks Canada decide which herds count as cattle-free, so a faster, better-calibrated ancestry caller would change breeding and translocation decisions — but this deposit cannot supply the training examples.

more_or_better_data.why: The deposit holds zero individual genomes; neural local-ancestry methods are trained on thousands of simulated or real admixed individuals, while this study has about 212 animals and does not share their genotypes.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements of ancestry per animal are distributed; the only uncertainty estimate is the authors' own 1 Mb block jackknife, which is not in the files.

models_beatable.why: Ancestry_HMM is a 2017 hidden Markov model and neural alternatives beat such methods on human data, but beating it here would need per-individual read data this deposit does not contain.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: we cannot run Ancestry_HMM as a baseline on these animals without terabytes of raw reads, and the labels would be that baseline's own output.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train a sequence model to call cattle-versus-bison ancestry along bison chromosomes, replacing the Ancestry_HMM step. Dead because the deposit distributes only the hidden Markov model's reference panel (5,358,142 marker rows of pooled allele counts), no per-animal genotypes, and the only labels available are that same model's posterior probabilities.

effort.compute_note: Measured: the three gzipped files total 79 MB and the 5,358,142 x 7 table loads in about 0.5 GB of RAM; no estimate given for the raw-read alignment route because it is out of scope (301 SRA runs, terabytes).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the columns of the main deposited file: 7, none of them an individual animal. That alone kills the project in two minutes.

verdict_reason: The Dryad deposit is only the reference marker panel for Ancestry_HMM, not a modelling dataset: no per-individual genotypes (A3), no label column (A2), labels would be another model's output (A8), and the biological sample size is about 212 animals (A5).
